entry.title: Locally nilpotent polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}$
entry.summary: For a polynomial $u=u(x)$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $r\in\mathbb{Z}$, we consider the orbit of $u$ at $r$ denoted and defined by $\mathcal{O}_u(r):=\{u(r),u(u(r)),\ldots\}$. We ask two questions here: (i) what are the polynomials $u$ for which $0\in \mathcal{O}_u(r)$, and (ii) what are the polynomials for which $0\not\in \mathcal{O}_u(r)$ but, modulo every prime $p$, $0\in \mathcal{O}_u(r)$? In this paper, we give a complete classification of the polynomials for which (ii) holds for a given $r$. We also present some results for some special values of $r$ where (i) can be answered.
entry.arxiv:comment: 17 pages. Few edits throughout the entire paper and one newly added subsection. To appear in INTEGERS. arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2211.06760

entry.title: Locally nilpotent polynomials over $\mathbb{Z}$
entry.summary: For a polynomial $u(x)$ in $\mathbb{Z}[x]$ and $r\in\mathbb{Z}$, we consider the orbit of $u(x)$ at $r$, $\mathcal{O}_u(r):=\{u(r),u(u(r)),\ldots\}$. We ask two questions here: (i) what are the polynomials $u$ for which $0\in \mathcal{O}_u(r)$ and (ii) what are the polynomials for which $0\not\in \mathcal{O}_u(r)$ but, modulo every prime $p$, $0\in \mathcal{O}_u(r)$? In this paper we classify the polynomials for which (ii) holds. We also present some results for some special $r'$s for which (i) can be answered.
